label: Dense encoding-phase feature (original tokens + <DEL>)
explanation: Dense feature (active on ~54% of all steps) that fires mainly while the original sequence is being read in and at the <DEL> step: 73% of original-phase steps and 58% of <DEL> steps are active, versus 30% of copy-phase steps. The predicate phase <= 1 captures 83% of activation mass (dev P 0.71, R 0.76, F1 0.74). Magnitude depends on position. Activity is weak at t=0 (rate 0.50) and highest at original positions 2-5 (rate ~0.85, the largest share of mass). It falls off again for late original positions 7-8. The strongest activations (up to 8.5) come at early original positions just after a repeated token, e.g. j j 1. Input token identity has only a mild effect (l, g, x have somewhat higher rates). It still fires weakly on many copy-phase steps (17% of mass), more often near the end of the copy. It is also inactive on about 30% of original-phase steps, and no simple token or history variable separates those cases. Adding the last copy steps or restricting positions did not push F1 above ~0.74.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: l, g, x, i; input phase: 1, k, m, a; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: l, x, g, i; copy phase: l, x, g, w; input phase: -); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, t=3, t=4.
